n_basis_note: N2 is plotted as molecules and converted x2 to N atoms. Established by closure, not by the paper text: NO3 + NO2 + NH3 + 2 N2 = 49.9, 50.3 and 46.3 mM-N at 60, 75 and 90 min against 50 mM initial, whereas N2 taken 1:1 would leave 8%, 11% and 22% of N unaccounted for. Closure over all times is 0.93-1.12, so the paper's own scatter is about 10% (nitrate + nitrite alone exceed 50 mM at 15 min).

provenance.citation: Polatides C., Kyriacou G., J. Appl. Electrochem. 35 (2005) 421-427
provenance.notes: Digitized by Daniel with WebPlotDigitizer (wpd_datasets.csv in this folder). Negative digitized values clamped to 0. Sn85Cu15 (bronze) cathode, -2.0 V vs Ag/AgCl, 50 mM nitrate, 0-120 min. The paper's model is NO3 -> NO2 (k1) -> NH3 (k2) plus 2 NO2 -> N2 (k3, second order); the curves in its Fig. 3 are that model. Digitized values compared with the figure image by eye, not pixel-overlaid. CAUTION: the printed k2 = 1.76e-5 s^-1 does not reproduce the paper's own NH3 curve (simulated NH3 at 120 min is 2.2 mM against 20.3 digitized); 1.76e-4 s^-1 does (RMSE 1.5 mM), so the printed exponent is probably a typo. Our fit of the digitized data gives k1 = 4.2e-4 s^-1, k2 = 1.8e-4 s^-1, k3 = 4.3e-3 L mol^-1 s^-1 against the printed k1 = 4.9e-4 and k3 = 7.66e-3. Supporting electrolyte is stated as 0.1 M K2SO4 for the cyclic voltammetry; confirm it was the electrolysis electrolyte too.

conditions.electrolyte: 50 mM KNO3 (0.1 M K2SO4 supporting electrolyte per CV section; confirm)
conditions.notes: 40 mL Teflon cell split by a Nafion 117 membrane into two equal compartments, so about 20 mL catholyte (volume inferred from that). pH of the catholyte shifts basic during electrolysis. Not converted to RHE.
